note: Targets for the daily sweep. Each one is somewhere a document about these incidents could appear.
The sweep NEVER writes a record. It reports candidates, and a person decides what, if anything,
becomes evidence and at what confidence. That is not timidity: assigning a state requires judging
whether sources are actually independent and what a document does and does not establish, and an
automated feed that could set a state would be a way of laundering an unsourced claim into a fact.
kind: rss   — an item feed. New items are reported once, by link.
html  — a page. Reported when the text that matches a watch term changes.
pdf   — a PDF. Same, with the text extracted if a reader is available; otherwise by checksum.
url may contain {YYYY}, {MM}, {DD}, {DD.MM.YYYY} and {DDMMYYYY}, filled with the sweep's date.
A 404 on a dated URL is not an error: it means nothing was published there that day.

targets.label: Delhi High Court cause list for today
targets.why: The listing carries the cause title, the connected matters and the bench. This is how PROC-DEL-002 was established, and it is where the 11 September 2026 hearing will appear.

targets.label: Delhi High Court, latest judgments
targets.why: Orders appear here before the case-status search, which is behind a captcha. An order in W.P.(CRL) 2127/2026 would close OQ-004.

targets.label: NHRC press releases
targets.why: The Commission has not announced the suo motu proceeding on its own page. If it does, or if it reports on the Delhi Police response, it appears here first.

targets.label: Parliamentary library
targets.why: Answered questions are published here as PDFs. A Home Ministry answer would be the Union speaking on its own record about the force it controls. Unreachable from the machine this was written on; the sweep records whether that is still true.

targets.label: Bar & Bench
targets.why: Legal reporting carries hearings on the day they happen, usually before anything reaches a court website.

targets.label: News — Jantar Mantar and the police action
targets.why: Leads, not evidence. Something reported here is a pointer to a document worth going after.

targets.label: News — the two proceedings by name
targets.why: Named-case reporting is the earliest signal that an order has been passed.

targets.label: News — facial recognition and the surveillance question
targets.why: OQ-034 asks what database was matched against and whether a private company processed the data. Both are live questions before the Supreme Court.

targets.label: News — the Bihar incidents
targets.why: Bihar is the deadline-critical jurisdiction: no court has ordered preservation there, so nothing is interrupting any retention schedule.
